messages.subject: vectorizing user-defined distribution
parts:
Hi,

Suppose a 2-element vector (a,b) is multi_normal_cholesky(mu,L),
and another 2-element vector (alpha,beta) is calculated using
softmax as

alpha <- exp(a)/(exp(a)+exp(b)+1)
beta <- exp(b)/(exp(a)+exp(b)+1)

I need a distribution for this --- for reasons I won't go into
here, it makes sense to do it this way instead of parametrizing in
(a,b).

I wrote the code below (my first user-defined distribution!) and
it works, I just have a couple of questions:

1. the log det of the Jacobian needs to be added to the returned
real, instead of increment_log_prob -- is this correct? The manual
is not very specific but I thought that incrementing the log prob
manually would be bad (non-functional) style.

2. would this benefit for vectorization, and if yes, how to do it?
my guess is that it won't help since the costly part is the
Cholesky decomposition, that's why I am using this form.

Minimal code is here (and works fine):

functions {
real bivariate_softmax_normal_log(vector alphabeta, vector mu,
matrix L) {
real alpha; real beta; real gamma; //
1-alpha-beta vector[2] ab; // ~
multivariate_normal_cholesky(mu,L) alpha <- alphabeta[1]; beta
<- alphabeta[2]; gamma <- 1-alpha-beta; ab[1] <-
log(alpha)-log(gamma); ab[2] <- log(beta)-log(gamma); return
(multi_normal_cholesky_log(ab, mu, L) +
log(1/(alpha*beta)+(1/alpha+1/beta)/gamma));
}
} data {
int<lower=0> N; vector[2] alphabeta[N];
} parameters {
vector[2] mu; cholesky_factor_cov[2] L;
} model {
for (i in 1:N) {
alphabeta[i] ~ bivariate_softmax_normal(mu, L);
}
}

Best,

Tamas

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: vectorizing user-defined distribution
parts:
On Thursday, July 30, 2015 at 11:28:41 AM UTC-4, Tamas Papp wrote:
1. the log det of the Jacobian needs to be added to the returned
real, instead of increment_log_prob -- is this correct? The manual
is not very specific but I thought that incrementing the log prob
manually would be bad (non-functional) style.

A user-defined function that ends in _log gets parsed so that it is passed lp__ (the accumulated log-posterior) by reference. However, I prefer to return a real anyway so that such functions can be tested via expose_stan_functions().

2. would this benefit for vectorization, and if yes, how to do it?
my guess is that it won't help since the costly part is the
Cholesky decomposition, that's why I am using this form.

The multi_normal_cholesky sampling statement accepts an array of vectors as its random variable. You would just need to account for each observation's Jacobian.

Ben
